data.name: CommandNotRecognized
data.value: '{0}' is not recognized as an internal or external command, operable program or batch file.
data.comment: cmd's own wording, kept word for word because scripts match on it.

data.name: SyntaxIncorrect
data.value: The syntax of the command is incorrect.
data.comment: cmd's own wording, kept word for word.

data.name: PathNotFound
data.value: The system cannot find the path specified: {0}

data.name: FileNotFound
data.value: The system cannot find the file specified: {0}

data.name: FileNotFoundShort
data.comment: what dir says when the pattern matched nothing. cmd's own wording, capitals included.

data.name: RemoveTree
data.comment: asked before a directory goes with everything under it, the way cmd asks for rd /s.

data.name: CouldNotFind
data.comment: what del says. cmd's own wording, capitals included.

data.name: OneInputExpected
data.value: Only one input can be written to a file.

data.name: AlgorithmNotSupported
data.value: {0} is not supported by this Windows.
data.comment: the SHA3 family, which needs a recent enough Windows to be present at all.

data.name: InvalidSwitch
data.comment: cmd's own wording, dash included.

data.name: ColourExpected
data.value: A colour is two hexadecimal digits, background then foreground.

data.name: NoFilesFound
data.value: INFO: Could not find files for the given pattern(s).
data.comment: what where says when nothing matched. The wording is the one where.exe uses.

data.name: WhereDetailLine
data.comment: the size, date and time where.exe writes for /T, in its own column widths.

data.name: BuiltInMarker
data.comment: how where reports a name the shell handles itself rather than a file on disk.

data.name: FileNameExpectedAfter
data.value: a file name was expected after '{0}'.

data.name: EndOfLine
data.comment: how the end of the line is named inside a syntax message, where a word would otherwise be quoted.

data.name: DirectoryMarker
data.comment: what dir writes in the size column for a directory.

data.name: ItemMarker
data.comment: what dir writes for a shell item that is neither a folder to enter nor a file with a size, the Control Panel launcher on the desktop and its like.

data.name: JunctionMarker
data.comment: what dir writes for a directory junction, cmd's own wording.

data.name: SymlinkMarker
data.comment: a symbolic link to a file, cmd's own wording.

data.name: SymlinkDirectoryMarker
data.comment: a symbolic link to a directory, cmd's own wording. The D is part of it.

data.name: LinkTargetSuffix
data.comment: where a link points, written after its name the way dir writes it.

data.name: StreamLine
data.comment: one alternate data stream under the entry it belongs to. The width puts its size under the size column above.

data.name: ShellEntryLine
data.comment: one entry of a shell folder. The date is blank for a virtual place, which has none to give.

data.name: PropertyLine
data.comment: one property of an item. The name is padded by the caller, which knows the column width.

data.name: PropertyCount
data.comment: the summary of a props listing, counting only the properties that had something to say.

data.name: NoMatch
data.comment: reported when a name written as a pattern found nothing, on disk or in the namespace.

data.name: NoProperties
data.comment: reported when an item refuses to open its properties at all, which a few virtual places do.

data.name: RawPropertyKey
data.comment: a property key no handler has named, written as its format identifier and its number.

data.name: ShellItemCount
data.comment: the summary of a shell folder listing, where there are no bytes or free space to report.

data.name: FileCountSummary
data.comment: the alignments line the two summary rows up with each other, keep them.

data.name: DirectoryCountSummary
data.comment: the alignments line the two summary rows up with each other, keep them.

data.name: HelpHeader
data.value: Built in commands, everything else is looked for on PATH.

data.name: HelpTab
data.value: TAB cycles through the names that match, directories first and with a trailing separator.

data.name: HelpShiftTab
data.value: Shift+TAB goes back through them, ESC puts back what you had typed.

data.name: HelpAutoCd
data.value: A line that is nothing but the name of a directory changes to it.

data.name: TerminatePrompt
data.comment: the two letters offered here have to be the ones in YesKey and NoKey. The trailing space is deliberate.

data.name: YesKey
data.comment: the key that answers yes, and what is echoed when it is pressed. One character.

data.name: NoKey
data.comment: the key that answers no, and what is echoed for any other answer. One character.

data.name: VirtualTerminalOff
data.value: refused, escape sequences will be printed as text

data.name: VirtualTerminalHint
data.value: This console does not support it. A console with "Use legacy console" ticked never will, and neither does one older than Windows 10. Untick it in the console properties and open a new window.

data.name: NoConsole
data.value: There is no console here, the output is going somewhere else.

data.name: DescribeConsole
data.value: shows the console modes, which is what decides whether colour works.

data.name: TreeCannotBeKilled
data.value: Only the command itself can be ended here, anything it started will keep running.
data.comment: shown when there is no job behind the command, so the list above cannot be the whole story.

data.name: ProcessElevated
data.value: (running elevated, cannot be read from here)

data.name: ProductHeadline
data.comment: company, product and version, the shape cmd's own first line has.

data.name: BannerHeadline
data.comment: the first line the shell prints when it starts, product and version.

data.name: WindowsUnknown
data.comment: used only when the registry will not say which Windows this is.

data.name: LabelEdition
data.comment: these six labels are the ones Windows Settings uses under System, About. Match that translation.

data.name: SystemTypeAndProcessor
data.comment: the operating system width and the processor, joined the way Settings joins them.

data.name: ProcessArchitectureNote
data.comment: added only when the shell is not built for the same architecture as the Windows it is running on.

data.name: NameValueLine
data.comment: how set and alias list what they hold. The equals sign is the syntax they are typed with, not punctuation.

data.name: PathLine
data.comment: PATH is the name of the variable and is not translated.

data.name: HelpLine
data.comment: a command and what it does. The width lines the descriptions up with each other.

data.name: HistoryLine
data.comment: a number and the line that was typed.

data.name: NothingMeasured
data.value: Nothing was started, so there is nothing else to report.
data.comment: a built in was measured, which runs inside the shell and has no accounting of its own.

data.name: TreeNotMeasured
data.value: No job held this command, so anything it started is not counted here.

data.name: LabelCpuShare
data.comment: processor time against elapsed time, so more than 100 percent means it used more than one core.

data.name: ClipboardUnavailable
data.value: The clipboard could not be opened.
data.comment: another process was holding it for longer than we were prepared to wait.

data.name: ActPrompt
data.value: Act on which? all, a number, or nothing:

data.name: ActNeedsConsole
data.value: Choosing needs a console. Name the action with /k:c, /k:r or /k:t, and /f to skip the asking.

data.name: NumberedProcessLine
data.comment: a process in the list to choose from, numbered so a number can be typed instead of an id.

data.name: MatchLimit
data.comment: a fragment can match half of PATH, and each match costs a Restart Manager session.

data.name: ProcessLine
data.comment: a process id and what it is, in the list shown before anything is killed.

data.name: SpecificationLine
data.comment: a label already padded to the column width, and its value.

data.name: WideDirectory
data.comment: how dir /w says an entry is a directory, cmd's own brackets.

data.name: PressAnyKey
data.comment: what dir /p waits on, the wording cmd uses.

data.name: DirectoryEntryLine
data.comment: one row of a dir listing. The date pattern is part of it, so a language that writes dates the other way round changes it here.

data.name: KeysResult
data.comment: what the keys command reports, the line the editor ended up with and where the cursor sits in it.

data.name: DescribeAlias
data.value: shows the macros, or defines one as name=text.

data.name: DescribeBase64
data.value: encodes a file, or the text itself when the name is not one. /d decodes, /o: writes to a file, /w: wraps, /t forces text.

data.name: DescribeCd
data.value: shows the current directory, or changes to one. cd - goes back.

data.name: DescribeClip
data.value: shows everything on the clipboard, or sets it from a pipe or from what follows. /v pastes text, /f writes the item paths, /c clears, /m watches.

data.name: ClipboardNoItems
data.value: The clipboard names no file or shell item.

data.name: NotRendered
data.comment: a format the owner offers but would only produce on demand, and it declined to.

data.name: DragContextValue
data.comment: the undocumented DragContext format the shell writes while dragging.

data.name: DescribeColor
data.value: sets the screen colours, two hexadecimal digits.

data.name: DescribeComplete
data.value: shows what TAB would offer for the rest of the line.

data.name: DescribeCopy
data.value: copies files. /y overwrites without asking, /-y always asks.

data.name: DescribeDel
data.value: deletes files. /s recurses, /f clears the read only attribute, /p asks each time, /q asks nothing, /a: selects by attribute.

data.name: DescribeDir
data.value: lists a directory. /b bare, /w and /d in columns, /p a screenful at a time, /s recurses, /a: selects by attribute, /o sorts, /t: picks the time, /l lowercases, /q owners, /x short names, /r data streams.

data.name: DescribeExit
data.value: ends the shell, with an exit code if one is given.

data.name: DescribeGuid
data.value: generates GUIDs. A number says how many, /f: picks the format N D B P X, /u uppercases.

data.name: DescribeHash
data.value: hashes a file, or the text itself when the name is not one. /a: picks the algorithm, /f: hex or base64, /u uppercases, /t forces text.

data.name: DescribeHistory
data.value: shows the command history. -c clears it.

data.name: DescribeKeys
data.value: runs a key script through the line editor and shows the result.

data.name: DescribeLock
data.value: shows which processes are holding something open. A name with no path is looked for among what is loaded. /m watches, /k closes them, /f asks nothing.

data.name: DescribeMeasure
data.value: runs a command and reports what it cost, in time, processor, memory, disk and graphics card. /p leaves out what it started.

data.name: DescribeMd
data.value: creates directories, including any missing parent.

data.name: DescribeMove
data.value: moves files and directories. /y overwrites without asking, /-y always asks.

data.name: DescribePopd
data.value: returns to the directory pushd left.

data.name: DescribePrompt
data.value: shows or sets the prompt, using cmd's $ codes.

data.name: DescribePushd
data.value: remembers the current directory and changes to another.

data.name: DescribeRd
data.value: removes directories. /s removes the contents too, /q does it without asking.

data.name: DescribeRen
data.value: renames a file or a directory in place.

data.name: DescribeSet
data.value: shows or sets variables. set /p name=text reads one in, set /a works one out.

data.name: DescribeStart
data.value: starts a program in a console of its own, or opens a document.

data.name: DescribeTitle
data.value: shows or sets the window title, which follows the current directory until you set one.

data.name: TokenList
data.value: tokens, written {{Name}} and replaced every prompt: {0}
data.comment: the words a title may be written with. The spaces line it up under the description above it.

data.name: TitleAdministrator
data.comment: shown in the window title when the shell is elevated, the way the console host says it.

data.name: DescribeVer
data.value: shows what this Windows is, in as much detail as it will admit to.

data.name: DescribeProps
data.value: shows everything the shell knows about a file or a namespace item.

data.name: DescribeWhere
data.value: shows every place a name resolves to. /R searches a tree, /Q is the exit code only, /F quotes, /T adds size and date.

data.name: MonitorNeedsConsole
data.value: Watching needs a console to paint on.
